key_insight: Language models handle many materials calculations and physical explanations well but struggle with fine-grained state comparisons and quantitatively justified decisions.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-assisted materials discovery requires condition-aware reasoning and evidence updates that improve predictions without destabilizing previously accurate ones.
method: M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning on 200 tasks across ten research functions using aluminium and high-entropy alloys.
M2 evaluates agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20 tests initial forecasts and revisions of hidden responses as observations accumulate along scientific dependency chains.
evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, related literature improved selected estimates, while progressive observations calibrated some downstream responses but destabilized earlier accurate predictions.
watch_item: Condition and baseline mismatches can undermine knowledge transfer, so literature-assisted predictions need careful experimental-context checks.
paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
